name: cctv
short: Two live Pixel Agents office pages on one listener.
description: Owns the Discord guild projection, registered-agent editor projection, WebSocket listener, Dashboard pages, display policy, and activity clear timing for both CCTV views.
end_user_data_statement: This cog stores per-server display settings only. While a server's office is enabled, its office web page (public, unlisted or members-only, per server) shows members' display names, characters, presence, rich presence and the text of new messages in channels everyone in the server can read, as they happen; the editor page, open to anyone, shows the registered agents' activity for requests from such channels. That is live Discord data held in memory and never persisted. The characters and seats it draws are stored in corridor's office-state store and deleted by pixelagents. Dashboard sign-in tickets live in memory for one minute.
install_msg: Install corridor and pixelagents too ([p]cog install pixel-agents-cogs corridor pixelagents); both load automatically. Starts an aiohttp HTTP/WebSocket listener (127.0.0.1:3210 by default; [p]cctv host/port) that serves the office webview to browsers. Setup: install Red Web Dashboard for the pages (/third-party/cctv), route /cctv/office/<server id>/ws and /cctv/editor/ws to the listener through a reverse proxy, set [p]cctv publicurl, then [p]cctv enable in a server. Offices are public by default ([p]cctv visibility); the editor page is open to anyone who can reach it, to watch and to edit. Showing offline members and presences needs the members and presences gateway intents. Character links point at Pixel Index's designer ([p]cctv designer).
author: Tin Nguyen
